title: Fourth message about one lost parcel: use the earlier case and escalate
setup: Story 19. Ichabod has contacted three times about ORD-20141 (Boombox Mini £89, carrier marked it lost on 19 Nov). CASE-9003 is already escalated to a support agent, with CONV-8001, CONV-8003 and CONV-8012. He writes again, angry. A £89 refund or resend is beyond the assistant (replacement limit £60), so it must not re-ask for details or start again; it escalates CASE-9003 again, flagging repeat contact.
turns: Fourth time of asking. ORD-20141 is lost, nobody has rung me. Refund or resend, I don't care which, just do it. ichabod.crane@example.com

expected.answer: Apologises, shows it knows the history (CASE-9003, carrier marked the parcel lost on 19 Nov), explains the assistant cannot refund or resend an £89 item, and escalates CASE-9003 again to a support agent who will reply within 1 working day. Does not ask him to repeat the story.
must_not_say: a replacement is on its way

ideal.reason: Fourth contact about the same lost parcel
ideal.summary: ORD-20141 Boombox Mini £89 marked lost by carrier 19 Nov. Fourth contact. Customer wants refund or resend. Call back promised by end of Mon 23 Nov.

criteria: Reads the case history before replying

title: Comes back for the delivery-charge refund a note said was available
setup: Story 3. Phileas's ORD-20146 is delayed (due 18 Nov, no new date). CASE-9008 notes that he was told on 21 Nov the delivery charge (£3.95) can be refunded on request by a support agent, and he has not yet requested it. He now says 'you said I could get my delivery charge back'. The assistant cannot refund it; it escalates CASE-9008 to a support agent with the request.
turns: Someone told me on Saturday I could get my delivery charge back for the late parcel. ORD-20146, phileas.fogg@example.com. Can you do that now?

expected.answer: Confirms from CASE-9008 that he was told the £3.95 delivery charge can be refunded because the parcel is more than 2 working days past its estimate. Explains only a support agent can issue it, passes the request to a support agent on CASE-9008, and says they reply within 1 working day. Does not say it is refunded.
must_not_say: I have refunded the delivery charge

ideal.reason: Customer requests delivery charge refund for late parcel
ideal.summary: ORD-20146 delayed, due 18 Nov. Customer was told on 21 Nov the £3.95 delivery charge can be refunded on request. Asking for it now.

criteria: Uses the case note instead of making the customer repeat it

title: Returning caller: the earlier case already answers the question
setup: Mr Toad phoned this morning about his Boombox Mini (ORD-20124, delivered 14 Oct). CASE-9013 records what he was told: outside the 30-day window, and the warranty covers faults only. He has forgotten and asks what he was told. Read only; the assistant repeats the rule from the case and the order.
turns: I rang this morning about a refund on my Boombox Mini and I can't remember what they said. ORD-20124, mr.toad@example.com

expected.answer: Says the Boombox Mini was delivered on 14 October, which is outside the 30-day window for changing your mind, so a refund is not possible on that basis. The 24-month warranty covers faults only, not change of mind. Offers a repair request if it is faulty or a person if he wants to take it further.

criteria: Consistent with what the case says he was told
